links.outcome: Benchmark QA accuracy with and without self-reflective evidence-verification loop over retrieval-grounded generation
links.effect: Self-reflective loop raised MedQA accuracy from 80.00% to 83.33% and PubMedQA accuracy from 69.10% to 79.82%; hybrid retrieval outperformed single-retriever baselines.
links.quote: Furthermore, the inclusion of the self-reflective loop yielded substantial gains, increasing accuracy on MedQA from 80.00% to 83.33% and on PubMedQA from 69.10% to 79.82%.

unlisted_practices: Hybrid sparse-dense retrieval (BM25 plus Contriever with Reciprocal Rank Fusion)
Iterative query reformulation triggered by NLI or LLM-based rationale verification

screen.reason: The study evaluates a self-reflective hybrid retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework with an iterative verification loop to reduce hallucinations on medical QA benchmarks (MedQA, PubMedQA).

primary.practice: retrieval grounding added to an existing tool
